name: Eisteddfod

attributes.attribute: a Welsh festival of bards held each year near 1 August
the land where the festival gathers its poets

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The Eisteddfod is a Welsh festival. It ranks among the longest-lived of Celtic feasts. The fair of Ireland may match it. Each year the bards meet in a new Welsh town near the first of August. Scholars think the gathering began in the old Celtic age. Then poets trained in oral verse battled in song. The rite was reborn in 1860 as a national event. Yet records trace it to 1176. Poetry and music shape the day, and Welsh is heard almost alone.

okr.objective: Introduce the Eisteddfod as the long-held Welsh festival of verse.
key_results: It ranks among the oldest of Celtic festivals.
The gathering sits near the ancient feast of Lughnasa on 1 August.
It was rebuilt in 1860 but records reach back to 1176.
Welsh alone is heard at the meeting.
